recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Do not change current core MedicationStatement or Medication value sets for FHIR-7170; handle any future RxNorm preference in jurisdictional IGs or terminology guidance rather than universal core wording.
issue_request: FHIR-7170 asked to say MedicationStatement.medication would usually be an RxNorm clinical drug code in the US due to Meaningful Use; the accepted Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution rejected US-centric wording and required correcting the exemplar medication.code value set to SNOMED CT is-a 410942007.
initial_application: Jira says the issue was fixed in SVN 6684. Git commit 6ce87fde09500c2d61c86a07ac98f49037e7d747 maps to build@6684 and changed source/medication/valueset-medication-codes.xml from route-of-administration root 284009009 to SNOMED CT 410942007, matching the source correction in the FHIR-7170 resolution.
additional_context: Current MedicationStatement is active and binds MedicationStatement.medication by example through medication-statement-medication-codes, which includes the shared medication-codes ValueSet. Later Published issue FHIR-19294 changed the Medication SNOMED exemplar to is-a 763158003, and the combined branch already reconciles that current state. Core still links to RxNorm guidance from the terminology systems page, while direct community searches found no conflicting FHIR-7170 evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reverting the current Medication value set to 410942007 would contradict later final Pharmacy guidance, and adding US Meaningful Use/RxNorm preference text would contradict the FHIR-7170 resolution's universal-standard rationale.
